As an ADMINISTRATIVE ASSISTANT, GS-0303-7, you will: Maintains the appointment schedule for the HRO and the DHRO. Schedules appointments and meetings, independently, based upon personal knowledge of their workload and current issues of importance.

Advises the HRO and the DHRO of scheduled appointments and furnishes information from files or schedules briefings by others in preparation for scheduled meetings. Reschedules appointments when it is apparent that they cannot meet previous schedules. Attends meetings when required to maintain notes. Prepares required slides for meetings.

Receives visitors and telephone calls for the HRO. Assists in the development of policy letters. Coordinates draft policy with other staff directorates prior to submission for final review and approval.

Maintains personal contact with HRO employees, functional managers (Army and Air), NGB personnel, and State personnel to discuss administrative requirements and services. Provides technical advice and guidance and recommends methods and procedures where necessary.

Advises other administrative personnel of latest HRO directives regarding administrative procedures. Reviews incoming correspondence, publications, regulations, and directives.

Prepares and/or reviews outgoing correspondence from the office of the HRO or subordinate branches for grammar, construction, proper format, attachments, continuity of text, policy and procedural adherence, and compliance with the HRO viewpoint. Advises the originator of any discrepancies and provides necessary training.

Maintains office files of correspondence, directives, regulations, and other information. Maintains security of all keys and maintains appropriate records of keys issued to personnel. Performs duties as HRO Publications Officer.

Coordinates with both Army and Air Force publications sources to accomplish ordering, locating electronic publications, updating, and maintaining a current and complete publications library for the HRO. Submits work orders for repairs and maintenance on HRO office equipment and facilities. Performs other duties as assigned.
General Experience: Administrative or clerical experience, education, or training which demonstrates the candidate's ability to perform the duties of the position. Experience using computer and automation systems. Specialized Experience: Must have at least 12 months experience in the interpretation and application of regulations, procedures or laws.

Experience that provided a working knowledge of administrative functions. Experience demonstrating the ability to advise lower graded employees. Experience working independently and setting priorities with very little supervisory control.

Unsere Gründer bringen langjährige Erfahrung von SAP und aus dem Silicon Valley mit, und wir sind überzeugt: Ein lebendiges, gut organisiertes Büro ist der Schlüssel zu unserem gemeinsamen Erfolg 🚀

Du sorgst dafür, dass das Büro aufgeräumt und ordentlich ist (z. B. Spülmaschine ein- und ausräumen, Bilder aufhängen, Gemeinschaftsräume in Schuss halten)

Du sorgst dafür, dass sich jeder im Büro wohlfühlt, und bist eine wichtige Ansprechperson für unsere Mitarbeitenden.

Fließendes Englisch sowie Deutschkenntnisse mindestens auf C1-Niveau
Praktisches Geschick und die Bereitschaft, überall mit anzupacken, wo Unterstützung gebraucht wird
Freude am Umgang mit Menschen sowie ein gutes Organisationstalent

As an Office Manager, you will be responsible for developing, implementing, and maintaining a multitude of administrative and management programs supporting the posts of duty (PODs).

These duties include providing overall administrative management to professional and administrative staff, ensuring full support for administrative and litigation programs, managing databases, and supporting automation initiatives.

The Office Manager is also responsible for managing and overseeing subordinate staffs which may be located in multiple PODs.As an Office Manager, you will: Assists in directing all of the administrative/resources management activities necessary for the successful operation of assigned PODs, which may include support of Area Counsel(s), including budget management, personnel management and administration, facilities management, etc.

Identifies and analyzes problems and issues, resource utilization and constraints, and coordination of management controls. Prepares, maintains, and executes the financial plan involving all categories of expenditures.

Develops ad hoc and routine statistical analyses and management status reports, along with recommendations, for the Area Manager and Associate Chief Counsel (FM), for procedural and other changes necessary to adjust the work processes and staffing requirements of the FM POD staff to keep pace with the day-to-day needs of the Office of Chief Counsel.

Reviews, analyzes, makes recommendations, and/or develops contingency plans based on financial, analyses and reports. Identifies trends and anticipates any adverse impact on budget and/or work plans. This is not an all-inclusive list.

The selectee from this vacancy announcement will manage one of the following Cluster Chief Counsel Offices: Portland, OR Sacramento, CA
Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected.

See "Required Documents" for a list of document requirements for all employment authorities. Career Transition Assistance Program Current Chief Counsel Employee Current IRS Employee In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or experience requirements described below.

Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application.

To qualify for this position of Office Manager you must meet the qualification requirements listed below by the closing of this announcement: For GS-11: Specialized Experience: Your resume must detail at least one year of specialized experience which includes:- Gathering data to estimate resource requirements- Prepare in-depth report to track progress of current goals- Procure office resources to include contractor support services and office suppliesThis definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-09).

OR Education Substitution: You may substitute education for specialized experience as follows: Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree OR three full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree OR LL.M., if related.

OR Combination of Education and Experience: You may qualify by a combination of experience and education: Options for qualifying based on a combination are identified in the online questions. NOTE: If qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application package.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

One year of experience refers to full-time work; part-time work is considered on a prorated basis. To ensure full credit for your work experience, please indicate dates of employment by month/year, and indicate number of hours worked per week, on your resume.

Time in Grade Requirement for GS-11: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-09).

If selected for this position, you will serve as the assistant to the United States Attorney (USA) for the District of Arizona, providing a variety of technical and administrative support services. A confidential relationship is required between the incumbent and the USA.

Typical work assignments will include: Managing and overseeing the day-to-day activities of the immediate office of the USA. Exercising exclusive control over the USA's calendar for all appointments, meetings, engagements, and conferences with complete authority for commitment of time.

Independently handling matters addressed to the USA that do not require personal attention by referring such to appropriate staff members, or personally performing the work needed to resolve the matter. Representing the USA when addressing leading figures with the government, business, law enforcement community, and other organizations.

Arranging conferences and meetings for the USA, preparing agendas and notifying participants. Developing a variety of recurring reports and documents which involve obtaining information from the staff, subject files or other sources, and formatting the needed information properly in narrative, table, or graph formats.

Producing a variety of written documents utilizing varied and advanced functions in one or more types of office automation software. Editing written material for adherence with supervisor's established policies, writing style, and previously expressed views, as well as for conformity with office policies and correspondence procedures.

Responsibilities will increase and assignments will become more complex as your training and experience progress.
GS-10: To be eligible at the GS-10 level, you must have at least ONE year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-9 level.

Specialized experience is defined as performing complex and confidential administrative support and tasks for superiors; maintaining and exercising control over supervisors' calendar for appointments, meetings, engagements and conferences; reading, screening and controlling incoming documents; receiving and screening visitors and callers; composing a variety of written material; ensuring accuracy of outgoing correspondence for procedural and grammatical accuracy; and making travel arrangements.

Trusted by startups backed by top-tier venture capital firms including Sequoia, a16z, Benchmark and Y Combinator, the team operates on a quality first, consultative model with a near 1:1 submit-to-hire ratio and 100+ successful placements. Their positioning is clear: top 1% talent, not volume.

About the Role This is a critical operational support role within the recruitment team. Reporting directly to the Operations Lead, you will provide end-to-end VA recruitment support across sourcing, candidate research, market mapping, documentation, and CRM administration. This is not a pure recruiter or sourcing-only role.

We are looking for someone with a VA mindset — strong recruitment operations experience, solid general admin capability, and the communication and initiative to thrive in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment. Key Responsibilities
· Source and research candidates across SaaS, Marketing, and IT sectors for US market roles
· Build and maintain talent pipelines through market mapping
· Maintain and update Recruit CRM with accurate candidate, role, and pipeline information
· Prepare and format candidate shortlists and summaries for the recruitment team
· Attend client intake calls as a note-taker — supporting the team, not leading calls
· Handle documentation, process notes, and general recruitment administration
· Liaise professionally with internal team members across US and international time zones
· Support ad hoc tasks as directed by the Operations Lead What You'll Bring Experience & Background
· Minimum 3–4 years of total experience, with at least 2 years in end-to-end recruiting or in a recruitment support capacity — in a VA context
· Industry background in SaaS, Marketing, or IT — healthcare and other unrelated experience is not a fit for this role
· Recent US market experience — you understand the nuances of recruiting for US-based clients A genuine mix of VA, general admin, and recruiting skills — not purely a sourcer or recruiter Communication & Personality
· Strong English — clear and confident in written and verbal communication
· Outspoken and direct — you proactively flag capacity issues and push back professionally when needed
· Flexible and adaptable — comfortable with shifting priorities and ad hoc tasks
· Polished, professional LinkedIn profile (reviewed as part of the selection process)

· Experience with Recruit CRM Bookkeeping or accounts reconciliation experience
· Familiarity with AI and automation tools — Claude Cowork or similar integration platforms
What Success Looks Like
· Consistent, high-quality sourcing output with minimal rework
· Proactive communication — status updates without prompting, blockers flagged early
· CRM and documentation kept current and accurate at all times
· Tasks completed within agreed timelines; clear escalation when timelines are at risk
· Smooth integration with the Operations Lead's workflow and the broader team Originally posted on Himalayas

You will play a key part in maintaining organization, improving productivity, and supporting important business decisions. Manage executive calendars, including scheduling meetings, appointments, and reminders

Coordinate meeting logistics including agendas, materials, and virtual setup
Take notes during meetings and distribute summaries or action items

4) Documentation and Administrative Support
Prepare, format, and organize documents, reports, and presentations

Strong verbal and written communication skills in English

The Administrative Assistant performs various administrative duties for the Nursing team. Duties include but not limited to the following: Perform clerical duties related to final discharge of patient i.e. eligibility, travel, appointments, prescriptions, prosthetics, referrals and or follow up appointments.

File patient medical record results i.e. laboratory tests, x-rays, consultation and or medical reports as required. Initiate work order request for equipment to the engineering department for minor repairs. Coordinate/facilitate i.e. ongoing implementation, evaluation and effective use of the automated scheduling system as needed.

Assist Management or Business Manager with compiling and/or retrieving pertinent reports and worksheets from the automated scheduling system. Create/maintain database for effective and efficient tracking and/or scheduling system for staff as required.

Coordinate administrative aspects i.e. patient care unit, staffing scheduling and allocation of resources as required. Serve as the first line of communication for veterans and visitors by providing information and assistance as required. Compile data reports i.e. Daily Census, DSS mapping and leave usage as needed.

Maintain patient confidentiality in accordance with the Privacy Act. Maintain clean, safe and orderly work area in accordance with clinical guidelines. Organize/prioritize problem solving techniques in daily work activities as needed. Work Schedule: Full-time, 0600-1430 Monday - Friday Virtual: This is not a virtual position.

Position Description/PD#: Administrative Assistant/PD11794A Relocation/Recruitment Incentives: Not Authorized Permanent Change of Station (PCS): Not Authorized Financial Disclosure Report: Not required
To qualify for this position, applicants must meet all requirements by the closing date of this announcement, 08/13/2026. Time-In-Grade Requirement: Applicants who are current Federal employees and have held a GS grade any time in the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements by the closing date of this announcement.

For a GS-05 position you must have served 52 weeks at the GS-04. The grade may have been in any occupation, but must have been held in the Federal service. An SF-50 that shows your time-in-grade eligibility must be submitted with your application materials.

If the most recent SF-50 has an effective date within the past year, it may not clearly demonstrate you possess one-year time-in-grade, as required by the announcement. In this instance, you must provide an additional SF-50 that clearly demonstrates one-year time-in-grade.

Note: Time-In-Grade requirements also apply to former Federal employees applying for reinstatement as well as current employees applying for Veterans Employment Opportunities Act of 1998 (VEOA) appointment.

You may qualify based on your experience and/or education as described below: Specialized Experience: You must have one year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade GS-04 in the normal line of progression for the occupation in the organization.

Examples of specialized experience would typically include, but are not limited to: Managing and organizing patient information, Performing administrative duties, and Providing customer service to patients in a medical care setting. OR, Education: Applicants may substitute education for the required experience.

To qualify based on education for this grade level you must have 4 years above high school. OR, Combination: Applicants may also combine education and experience to qualify at this level. You must have an combination of specialized experience and 4 years above high school worth of education.

For more information on these qualification standards, please visit the United States Office of Personnel Management's website at https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/.

What we need from you.
Excellent written and spoken English (clear, professional, and confident).
Fast, sound decision-making —you can choose between good options quickly and confidently.
Genuine satisfaction in getting things in order —you naturally improve clarity, organization, and follow-through.
Communication preference : a strong preference for calling over emailing, especially when resolution is faster by phone.
Problem-solving style : when you bring a problem, you also bring three solutions for the founder to choose from.
People interaction comfort : you are willing to talk with clients/partners and coordinate accordingly.
Not a fit if: you want part-time hours, you require a real estate license as a condition of the role, or you’d rather not talk to people.
Schedule & training: full-time hours set in your local time. You receive personalized training directly from the founder during your first weeks.
Trial: a two-week paid trial period before either of us commits.
You will own the founder’s calendar and build the week—deciding what’s scheduled, what’s rescheduled, and what needs immediate attention.
Manage the inbox end-to-end: you read incoming mail first and handle about nine of every ten messages without the founder.
Track open items across the business and drive them to closure, keeping status clear and up to date.
Work alongside our AI system by reviewing and approving what it proposes before anything is sent externally.
Build and maintain operational playbooks that standardize how we work and why our processes pay off.
Handle time-sensitive communication with quick, sound judgment and consistent follow-through.
Provide thoughtful escalation when a decision must be made by the founder—typically after you’ve offered the best options.

* Using good laboratory practices, statistical methods, and accredited quality requirements to strengthen compliance and continuous improvement.
* Collaborating with a service-oriented mindset, clear communication, strong organization, and the initiative to solve problems efficiently.
* Communicating fluently in English.
* Bringing collaboration, fresh thinking, bold questions, respect, and a positive, wellbeing-oriented mindset, to create shared value.

We are committed to an inclusive and respectful hiring experience and are happy to provide reasonable accommodations if needed. Our workplaces are fully accessible and supported by a strong safety culture, with modern installations and procedures to ensure a safe environment for everyone.
